fields.description: Clone runs `bench get-app` to bring a repository into the bench for the first time. Pull runs `git pull` inside an app already there. Command runs one of the catalogued bench commands. SSL issues or renews a Let's Encrypt certificate. They are different enough that the choice is always explicit rather than inferred from which fields happen to be filled in.
fields.label: Operation

fields.description: For a Pull this is the app directory inside the bench. For a Clone it is derived from the repository name and passed to bench explicitly, so bench never has to guess it from a URL carrying an SSH host alias.
fields.label: App

fields.description: Leave blank to use the repository's default branch for a Clone, or the branch the app is already on for a Pull.
fields.label: Branch

fields.description: A profile supplies the account, the SSH host alias and the token used to list repositories. Use Git URL for a remote that is not on one of your profiles.
fields.label: Source Type

fields.description: Just the repository name, e.g. gh_erp — not the full URL.
fields.label: Repository

fields.description: A full git remote, e.g. git@github.com:org/repo.git
fields.label: Git URL

fields.description: The exact remote that will be cloned, after any host alias is applied.
fields.label: Resolved URL

fields.description: Leave this on. Building assets is by far the largest memory consumer in a bench operation and the step most likely to take a small server down. Run `bench build --app <name>` by hand when the box is idle.
fields.label: Skip Asset Build

fields.description: If the app directory already exists, replace it. bench ARCHIVES the old copy to archived/apps/<name>-<date> rather than deleting it, so nothing is lost.
fields.label: Overwrite If Present

fields.description: By default a Pull is --ff-only, so it refuses rather than inventing a merge commit when the branch has diverged. Tick this only if you know the divergence is expected and a merge is what you want.
fields.label: Allow Merge Commit

fields.description: For a Clone, optionally run `bench --site <site> install-app` afterwards. For a site-scoped Command, the site it runs against. Leave blank on a Clone to only place the code on disk.
fields.label: Site

fields.description: Passes --force to install-app. Only needed when reinstalling an app the site already has.
fields.label: Force Install

fields.description: “Completed With Warnings” means the work was done but the command still exited non-zero. The case this exists for: bench finishes a get-app by calling `sudo supervisorctl status`, which fails on a host with no passwordless sudo — the app is cloned and installed, and only the cosmetic restart failed. Reporting that as Failed invites a re-run, and a re-run needs --overwrite, which archives the app that was already fine.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Draft
Queued
Running
Success
Completed With Warnings
Failed
Cancelled

fields.description: The authoritative success signal — 0 succeeded, above 0 the command failed, -1 means it never ran because a pre-flight refused it. stdout and stderr are interleaved in the log for readability, so the log text can never be used to decide whether it worked.
fields.label: Exit Code

fields.description: The exact argv that was executed, so it can be reproduced by hand in a terminal.
fields.label: Command

fields.description: Identifier from the catalogue in server/bench/commands.py. Commands are never assembled from free text — the argv comes from a fixed entry plus parameters matched against a pattern.
fields.label: Command

fields.description: JSON of the values supplied for this command's parameters, each validated against the pattern its catalogue entry declares.
fields.label: Command Parameters

fields.description: Issue Or Reinstall runs `bench setup lets-encrypt <site> -n`, which stops nginx, asks Let's Encrypt for a certificate and writes it into the site config. Renew drives certbot directly rather than `bench renew-lets-encrypt`, because that command asks for confirmation and cannot be answered by a background job.
fields.label: SSL Operation

fields.description: Leave empty to certify the site's own domain. Set it to certify one of the extra domains already configured for the site — it must already be listed there, and it must resolve to this server before Let's Encrypt will issue anything.
fields.label: Custom Domain

fields.description: Rehearse the renewal against Let's Encrypt's staging server. Nothing is installed. Worth doing first: Let's Encrypt rate-limits failures per IP and the block outlasts the mistake, so a rehearsal is cheaper than being locked out.
fields.label: Dry Run

fields.description: Identifies one backup set — the timestamp and site name frappe shares across the database dump, the files tars and the site_config snapshot. The individual paths are resolved from disk when the job runs, so a set that has been rotated away is caught before anything is dropped rather than after.
fields.label: Backup Set

fields.description: Run `bench backup` immediately before restoring. bench restore drops the database and there is no undo, and the moment you want a backup is the moment it is already gone. Leave this on unless you have just taken one yourself.
fields.label: Back Up First

fields.description: Restore the public files tar from the same backup set, if it has one.
fields.label: Restore Public Files

fields.description: Restore the private files tar from the same backup set, if it has one.
fields.label: Restore Private Files

fields.description: Database super user. Left empty this is "root", which is almost always right.
fields.label: Database Root Username

fields.description: Required. bench restore needs the database super user to drop and recreate the site database, and without it frappe asks on a terminal a background job does not have. Stored encrypted, cleared once the job finishes, and redacted out of the command that is logged.
fields.label: Database Root Password

fields.description: Only for an encrypted backup. It is the `encryption_key` from the site config of the server the backup was taken on — an encrypted dump cannot be restored without it.
fields.label: Backup Encryption Key
